name: Fern Lin
life: “I still remember a colleague giving me exactly one fact before handing over a voice.” Thursday often includes a stop at the bank steps, where Fern takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I took the second call and inherited the trust the first voice had built. I want the writer to hear both names.
appearance: Fern is easy to recognize by a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow and a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Usually dressed in a pale blue work shirt with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it, Fern rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket when listening.
personality: Fern talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Fern's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
family: Stella Choi is Fern’s cousin. Fern offers the first invitation. Stella gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *A house divided kindly*, Stella says, “I used to squeeze through the gap to see my best friend.”
connections: Imani Ford (first call taker). Restoring both voices to the letter is their first shared task after the interrupted call.
